title: The Hospital That Used Radiation to 'Treat' Acne—It Gave Teens Cancer
hook: In the 1950s, doctors exposed thousands of teenagers to high-dose radiation for acne—decades later, their faces literally rotted away.
why_this_can_go_viral: Juxtaposes a common teenage problem with horrific long-term effects; survivors' photos are visceral and shareable.

title: The Pharmaceutical CEO Who Buried Evidence of a Lethal Birth Defect
hook: He knew his anti-nausea drug caused babies to be born without limbs—but he ordered the files shredded and kept selling it.
why_this_can_go_viral: Thalidomide is known but the CEO-level cover-up story is less told; babies with no arms trigger outrage and clicks.

title: The Doctor Who Injected Polio Into Healthy Kids—To See What Would Happen
hook: He wasn't testing a vaccine—he was trying to give children polio, on purpose, in a secret ward hidden from parents.
why_this_can_go_viral: Pure evil experimentation on children is maximum dark curiosity; the 'hidden ward' detail is cinematic.

title: The 'Cancer Cure' That Was Just Baking Soda and Prayer
hook: He sold it for $10,000 a bottle—and convinced terminal patients to throw away their chemotherapy for a kitchen ingredient.
why_this_can_go_viral: Anger at preying on the desperate combined with the absurdity of a common kitchen item being sold as a cure.

title: The Hospital That Charged $10,000 for an Aspirin—And Got Away With It
hook: A patient got a bill for $10,000 for a single aspirin, and the hospital argued it was 'standard pricing'—then sued her for non-payment.
why_this_can_go_viral: Modern relatable rage—everyone has had an insane medical bill; the aspirin example is absurdly shareable.

title: The Government That Knew a Deadly Virus Was Spreading—But Called It 'Pneumonia'
hook: They suppressed the real diagnosis for months because acknowledging the outbreak would hurt tourism—thousands died.
why_this_can_go_viral: Parallels to recent events drive engagement; the 'tourism over lives' angle is infuriating and memorable.

title: The Doctor Who Tested Experimental Vaccines on Kids in Orphanages
hook: He told the nuns they were 'vitamin shots'—but they were live smallpox vaccines, and dozens of children died in agony.
why_this_can_go_viral: Innocence betrayed in a setting of trust (orphanage/nuns) creates maximum emotional impact and moral outrage.

title: The 'Cure for Diabetes' That Was Just Rat Poison—And Killed Hundreds
hook: It was sold as a natural herbal remedy; in reality, it was laced with a rodenticide that destroyed kidneys and livers.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exploits the 'natural vs pharmaceutical' debate—people die trusting 'natural' labels; shocking and cautionary.

title: The Hospital System That Billed for Surgeries on Dead Patients—For Decades
hook: They kept billing Medicare for hip replacements, heart surgeries, and amputations—years after the patients were buried.
why_this_can_go_viral: Absurd crime that is both dark and funny; 'posthumous surgery' is a shocking concept that spreads as a WTF story.

title: The 'Safe' Sunscreen That Gave Everyone Chemical Burns
hook: It was FDA-approved and sold in every pharmacy—until people's skin started blistering and peeling off after one application.
why_this_can_go_viral: Summer-related and universally used product—every sunscreen user will click to see if theirs is safe.

title: The Nurse Who Replaced Patients' IV Fluids With Poison—For Fun
hook: She worked in the ICU and swapped saline bags with a toxic chemical—then watched as patients died in front of her eyes.
why_this_can_go_viral: True crime medical horror is a proven viral category; the 'for fun' detail is chilling and click-maximizing.

title: The Drug Company That Sold 'Generic' Meds—They Were Placebo Sugar Pills
hook: Patients took their 'medication' for years; their conditions worsened and some died—while the company pocketed millions making candy.
why_this_can_go_viral: Betrayal of trust in generic medication affects everyone; the 'candy instead of cure' angle is outrageously shareable.

title: The Doctor Who Implanted Patients With Sewer Bacteria—For 'Gut Health'
hook: He performed fecal transplants using raw sewage from the city treatment plant—patients got septic shock and organ failure.
why_this_can_go_viral: Disgust and horror combined with a trendy health topic (gut microbiome); visceral reaction drives shares.

title: The 'All-Natural' Supplement That Contained Window Cleaner
hook: It was labeled as organic herbal extract—laboratory tests found it was 30% window cleaning fluid and 70% sawdust.
why_this_can_go_viral: Outrage at 'natural' label deception; the sawdust detail is absurd and memorable—great for short-form shock.

title: The Government That Hid an Anthrax Outbreak—To Avoid Panic
hook: A factory leaked anthrax spores over a town; officials told residents the strange deaths were 'flu'—and hundreds got sick.
why_this_can_go_viral: Post-COVID distrust of official narratives makes this highly resonant; 'they lied about anthrax' is explosive.

title: The Pharmaceutical Company That Sold a 'Cancer Vaccine'—It Was Sugar Water
hook: They charged $50,000 per dose to desperate families—and the 'vaccine' was literally sugar, water, and food coloring.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exploiting dying people is maximum moral outrage; the simple ingredient reveals the depth of the scam.

title: The Surgeon Who Operated on the Wrong Side of the Brain—Then Lied About It
hook: He drilled into the healthy side of a patient's skull, then told the family the tumor 'mysteriously disappeared'—the patient died.
why_this_can_go_viral: Incompetence + cover-up is a powerful combo; the absurd lie ('tumor disappeared') adds dark humor that boosts shares.
